messages.subject: DSM: obsdata doubts
parts:
Hello everyone, 

I'm working with wild guanacos and I intend to use dsm in the data collected but some doubts raised when preparing the observation data.
In some case cases, many observations fell in the same segment. For example, in one segment I have two observations: the first one is of 2 animals and the second, 5 animals.
Is the obsdata a summary of all the observations in one segment or should I leave all the information?
I imagine that if the first choice is correct the obsdata will have a row per segment with the sum of all the observations in that segment (in the example, it would be size=7). But if the second choice is correct I will have as many rows of the same segment as observations from that segment
Sample.label       Size
segment1               2 
segment 1              5

Thank you very much in advance!


Antonella

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSM: obsdata doubts
parts:
Antonella

It is my understanding that an observation is equivalent to a detection.  You saw two clusters of animals in a single segment, treat them separately.  Multiple rows per segment is fine.
